mappings.note: PA = PB makes triangle PAB isosceles and fixes angle PAB (LO-3); the 90 degrees between OA and the tangent then gives angle OAB (LO-2). Both theorems are used in sequence, so both are cited.
The angle between the tangents and the angle between the radii are supplementary because each contact angle is 90 degrees. No length equality is used, so LO-2.

Recall of the definition of a SECANT - a line meeting a circle in two points. It sits with the chord half of LO-4 for want of anywhere better; the fit is weak because the frame has no vocabulary or definition outcome and LO-4 speaks of solving problems.
Supplementary tangent and radii angles from the two right angles, then an isosceles triangle on two radii. Perpendicularity drives it; the equal tangent lengths are not needed.
The 90 degrees at the contact plus the bisected central angle gives angle OPA from the angle sum of a right triangle.
Tangent length from the right triangle on radius and centre distance. The item is a bare statement of the LO-2 consequence, with a single tangent.
PA perpendicular to PB together with the two right angles at the contacts makes CAPB a square, so each tangent equals the radius. Every angle used is a contact right angle, so LO-2 leads.
KN = AK + BN follows from KA = KM and NB = NM, two applications of equal tangents from the external points K and N. No angle or right triangle enters.
The right angle at Q plus the exterior-angle relation at O gives angle OPQ. Single tangent, so no equal-length argument is available.
The tangent length comes out of the right triangle OAP (LO-2), but halving the 60 degrees first requires that OP bisects the angle, which rests on the two tangents being equal (LO-3).
PQ = PR are equal tangents to the INNER circle (LO-3), and PS is then doubled because the inner radius meets PS at right angles and bisects it (LO-2). Two circles, two theorems.

The answer is an angle at the circumference on chord QR, reached from the central angle that the two tangents determine. Tangents plus a chord angle, so LO-4. Stem carries no data whatever - the 60 degrees exists only in the figure, so it cannot be answered as printed.
PA = PB makes PAB isosceles, and the 60 degree apex makes it equilateral, so the chord equals the tangent length. The equal-tangents property is what produces the isosceles triangle.
Right triangle OAT from the perpendicular at the contact, then a cosine. Duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter with the same numbers.
Asks both the chord-radius angle and the TANGENT-CHORD angle at P, which is LO-4's subject. The central angle it needs (70 degrees) is only in the figure, so the printed stem is incomplete.
Incircle of a triangle: AP = AR and CQ = CR let BC be assembled from the given segments. Equal tangents throughout, with no angle work.

Proves that a chord of the outer circle touching the inner one is BISECTED at the contact point - which holds precisely because the inner radius is perpendicular to it there. A direct corollary of LO-2.
Circumscribed quadrilateral, AD recovered from AB + CD = BC + AD via equal tangent segments at the four vertices.
OP = 2PS needs both: the bisection of the 120 degrees relies on the tangents from P being equal (LO-3), and the 30-60-90 triangle relies on the right angle at S (LO-2).
Angle OAB is the contact right angle minus the given angle PAB, then an isosceles triangle on two radii. The perpendicularity is what converts the given angle into a usable one.
Uses the central-versus-circumference angle on arc AQ before the tangent right angle is applied. The chord/arc angle relation is the distinguishing step, which is LO-4 rather than plain LO-2.
The statement of LO-3 itself, proved by congruent right triangles. This is the outcome's own theorem, so nothing else competes.

A CHORD equal to the radius makes POQ equilateral and fixes the central angle, from which the tangent angle follows. The chord length driving an angle is LO-4's territory; LO-2 supplies only the supplementary step.
OR = PR + RQ needs the bisection of the 120 degrees from the equal tangents (LO-3) and the right angle at the contact for the 30-60-90 ratio (LO-2).
Ends on an angle at the circumference standing on chord TQ, obtained from the central angle the tangents determine. Tangents plus a chord angle - LO-4.
